sanskrit: visṛjya lakṣmaṇaṃ rāmo duḥkhaśokasamanvitaḥ purodhasaṃ mantriṇaś ca naigamāṃś cedam abravīt
english: Having dismissed Lakṣmaṇa, Rāma, filled with grief and sorrow, addressed the chaplain, the ministers, and the citizens thus:

sanskrit: adya rājye 'bhiṣekṣyāmi bharataṃ dharmavatsalam ayodhyāyāṃ patiṃ vīraṃ tato yāsyāmy ahaṃ vanam
english: "Today I shall consecrate Bharata, devoted to dharma, the heroic lord of Ayodhyā, to the kingdom; thereafter I myself shall depart to the forest."

sanskrit: praveśayata saṃbhārān mā bhūt kālātyayo yathā adyaivāhaṃ gamiṣyāmi lakṣmaṇena gatāṃ gatim
english: "Bring in the consecration materials so that no time be lost — today itself I shall go the way that Lakṣmaṇa has gone."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā rāghaveṇoktaṃ sarvāḥ prakṛtayo bhṛśam mūrdhabhiḥ praṇatā bhūmau gatasattvā ivābhavan
english: Hearing what Rāghava had spoken, all the subjects bowed their heads deeply to the ground and became as though bereft of life.

sanskrit: bharataś ca visaṃjño 'bhūc chrutvā rāmasya bhāṣitam rājyaṃ vigarhayām āsa rāghavaṃ cedam abravīt
english: Bharata too lost consciousness upon hearing Rāma's words; he denounced the kingdom and spoke thus to Rāghava:

sanskrit: satyena hi śape rājan svargaloke na caiva hi na kāmaye yathā rājyaṃ tvāṃ vinā raghunandana
english: "By truth I swear, O king — not even in the heavenly world do I desire the kingdom without you, O joy of the Raghu lineage."

sanskrit: imau kuśīlavau rājann abhiṣiñca narādhipa kosaleṣu kuśaṃ vīram uttareṣu tathā lavam
english: "Anoint these two bards, Kuśa and Lava, O king, lord of men — the heroic Kuśa over the Kosalas, and Lava over the northern realm."

sanskrit: śatrughnasya tu gacchantu dūtās tvaritavikramāḥ idaṃ gamanam asmākaṃ svargāyākhyāntu māciram
english: "Let swift-striding messengers go to Śatrughna and without delay announce to him this departure of ours to heaven."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā bharatenoktaṃ dṛṣṭvā cāpi hy adho mukhān paurān duḥkhena saṃtaptān vasiṣṭho vākyam abravīt
english: Hearing what Bharata had said, and seeing the citizens downcast and burning with sorrow, Vasiṣṭha spoke these words:

sanskrit: vatsa rāma imāḥ paśya dharaṇīṃ prakṛtīr gatāḥ jñātvaiṣām īpsitaṃ kāryaṃ mā caiṣāṃ vipriyaṃ kṛthāḥ
english: "Dear Rāma, behold — all these subjects have prostrated themselves on the earth. Knowing what they desire and require, do not act contrary to their wishes."

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhasya tu vākyena utthāpya prakṛtījanam kiṃ karomīti kākutsthaḥ sarvān vacanam abravīt
english: At Vasiṣṭha's words, Kākutstha raised up the assembled subjects and addressed them all, asking: "What shall I do?"

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvāḥ prakṛtayo rāmaṃ vacanam abruvan gacchantam anugacchāmo yato rāma gamiṣyasi
english: Then all the subjects spoke to Rāma: "We shall follow you wherever you go, O Rāma."

sanskrit: eṣā naḥ paramā prītir eṣa dharmaḥ paro mataḥ hṛdgatā naḥ sadā tuṣṭis tavānugamane dṛḍhā
english: "This is our supreme joy; this is deemed our highest dharma; the satisfaction dwelling in our hearts is always firm in following you."

sanskrit: paureṣu yadi te prītir yadi sneho hy anuttamaḥ saputradārāḥ kākutstha samaṃ gacchāma satpatham
english: "If you have love and unsurpassed affection for your citizens, then, O Kākutstha, lead us along the true path together with our sons and wives."

sanskrit: tapovanaṃ vā durgaṃ vā nadīm ambhonidhiṃ tathā vayaṃ te yadi na tyājyāḥ sarvān no naya īśvara
english: "Whether to a forest of austerities, or a stronghold, or a river, or the ocean — if we are not to be abandoned by you, lead us all, O Lord."

sanskrit: sa teṣāṃ niścayaṃ jñātvā kṛtāntaṃ ca nirīkṣyaca paurāṇāṃ dṛḍhabhaktiṃ ca bāḍham ity eva so 'bravīt
english: He, knowing their resolve, and perceiving the decree of fate as well as the citizens' unwavering devotion, said simply: "So be it."

sanskrit: evaṃ viniścayaṃ kṛtvā tasminn ahani rāghavaḥ kosaleṣu kuśaṃ vīram uttareṣu tathā lavam
english: Having made this decision, on that very day Rāghava consecrated the heroic Kuśa over the Kosalas and Lava over the northern realm —

sanskrit: abhiṣiñcan mahātmānāv ubhāv eva kuśīlavau rathānāṃ tu sahasrāṇi trīṇi nāgāyutāni ca
english: — anointing both those great-souled princes, Kuśa and Lava; and he gave to each three thousand chariots, ten thousand elephants,

sanskrit: daśa cāśvasahasrāṇi ekaikasya dhanaṃ dadau bahuratnau bahudhanau hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanāvṛtau
english: and ten thousand horses as gift to each — endowing both with abundant jewels and great wealth, surrounded by joyful and prosperous people.

sanskrit: abhiṣicya tu tau vīrau prasthāpya svapure tathā dūtān saṃpreṣayām āsa śatrughnāya mahātmane
english: Having consecrated those two heroes and dispatched them to their own cities, he then sent swift messengers to the great-souled Śatrughna.

sanskrit: te dūtā rāmavākyena coditā laghuvikramāḥ prajagmur madhurāṃ śīghraṃ cakrur vāsaṃ na cādhvani
english: Those messengers, urged by Rāma's command and swift of stride, proceeded quickly to Madhurā and did not halt on the way.

sanskrit: tatas tribhir aho rātraiḥ saṃprāpya madhurām atha śatrughnāya yathāvṛttam ācakhyuḥ sarvam eva tat
english: Then, arriving at Madhurā within three days and nights, they reported to Śatrughna everything exactly as it had occurred:

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇasya parityāgaṃ pratijñāṃ rāghavasya ca putrayor abhiṣekaṃ ca paurānugamanaṃ tathā
english: — the abandonment of Lakṣmaṇa, Rāghava's resolve, the consecration of his two sons, and likewise the citizens' intention to follow him.

sanskrit: kuśasya nagarī ramyā vindhyaparvatarodhasi kuśāvatīti nāmnā sā kṛtā rāmeṇa dhīmatā
english: The charming city of Kuśa, established on the slopes of the Vindhya mountains by the wise Rāma, was named Kuśāvatī.

sanskrit: śrāvitā ca purī ramyā śrāvatīti lavasya ca ayodhyāṃ vijanāṃ caiva bharataṃ rāghavānugam
english: And the beautiful city of Lava was proclaimed Śrāvatī; and Ayodhyā was left deserted, with Bharata following Rāghava.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarvaṃ nivedyāśu śatrughnāya mahātmane viremus te tato dūtās tvara rājann iti bruvan
english: Having thus swiftly reported everything to the great-souled Śatrughna, those messengers then fell silent, saying: "Hasten, O king."

sanskrit: śrutvā taṃ ghorasaṃkāśaṃ kulakṣayam upasthitam prakṛtīs tu samānīya kāñcanaṃ ca purohitam
english: Hearing of this dreadful-seeming dissolution of the lineage now at hand, he assembled his subjects and his chaplain Kāñcana,

sanskrit: teṣāṃ sarvaṃ yathāvṛttam ākhyāya raghunandanaḥ ātmanaś ca viparyāsaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
english: and, as a joy of the Raghu line, he narrated to them everything that had taken place and the reversal of his own fortune that was to come, along with his brothers.

sanskrit: tataḥ putradvayaṃ vīraḥ so 'bhyaṣiñcan narādhipaḥ subāhur madhurāṃ lebhe śatrughātī ca vaidiśam
english: Then that heroic lord of men consecrated his two sons: Subāhu received Madhurā, and Śatrughnātī received Vaidiśā.

sanskrit: dvidhākṛtvā tu tāṃ senāṃ mādhurīṃ putrayor dvayoḥ dhanadhānyasamāyuktau sthāpayām āsa pārthivau
english: Dividing that army from Madhurā between his two sons, he established both princes well-stocked with wealth and grain.

sanskrit: tato visṛjya rājānaṃ vaidiśe śatrughātinam jagāma tvarito 'yodhyāṃ rathenaikena rāghavaḥ
english: Then, having bade farewell to the king Śatrughnātī at Vaidiśā, that Rāghava hastened to Ayodhyā in a single chariot.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa mahātmānaṃ jvalantam iva pāvakam kṣaumasūkṣmāmbaradharaṃ munibhiḥ sārdham akṣayaiḥ
english: He saw the great-souled Rāma blazing like fire, clad in fine linen garments, accompanied by imperishable sages.

sanskrit: so 'bhivādya tato rāmaṃ prāñjaliḥ prayatendriyaḥ uvāca vākyaṃ dharmajño dharmam evānucintayan
english: He then saluted Rāma with palms joined and senses controlled, and spoke these words — he who knew dharma, meditating on dharma alone:

sanskrit: kṛtvābhiṣekaṃ sutayor yuktaṃ rāghavayor dhanaiḥ tavānugamane rājan viddhi māṃ kṛtaniścayam
english: "Having duly consecrated both the sons of the Rāghava line with proper gifts, know me, O king, as fully resolved to accompany you."

sanskrit: na cānyad atra vaktavyaṃ dustaraṃ tava śāsanam tyaktuṃ nārhasi māṃ vīra bhaktimantaṃ viśeṣataḥ
english: "There is nothing more to be said in this matter — your command is irresistible. You should not abandon me, O hero, especially as I am devoted to you."

sanskrit: tasya tāṃ buddhim aklībāṃ vijñāya raghunandanaḥ bāḍham ity eva śatrughnaṃ rāmo vacanam abravīt
english: Understanding his resolute and unfaltering mind, Rāma, the joy of the Raghus, said to Śatrughna simply: "So be it."

sanskrit: tasya vākyasya vākyānte vānarāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ ṛkṣarākṣasasaṃghāś ca samāpetur anekaśaḥ
english: At the conclusion of his speech, monkeys assuming any form at will, and multitudes of bears and rākṣasas, converged there in great numbers.

sanskrit: devaputrā ṛṣisutā gandharvāṇāṃ sutās tathā rāma kṣayaṃ viditvā te sarva eva samāgatāḥ
english: Sons of gods, sons of sages, and sons of Gandharvas — all of them, knowing Rāma's dissolution was at hand, had all gathered together.

sanskrit: te rāmam abhivādyāhuḥ sarva eva samāgatāḥ tavānugamane rājan saṃprāptāḥ sma mahāyaśaḥ
english: All assembled, they saluted Rāma and said: "We have come, O king of great renown, desiring to accompany you."

sanskrit: yadi rāma vināsmābhir gacches tvaṃ puruṣarṣabha yamadaṇḍam ivodyamya tvayā sma vinipātitāḥ
english: "If you were to depart without us, O bull among men, it would be as though you had struck us down with the rod of Yama himself."

sanskrit: evaṃ teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā ṛṣkavānararakṣasām vibhīṣaṇam athovāca madhuraṃ ślakṣṇayā girā
english: Hearing those words of the bears, monkeys, and rākṣasas, he then spoke to Vibhīṣaṇa in gentle and sweet tones:

sanskrit: yāvat prajā dhariṣyanti tāvat tvaṃ vai vibhīṣaṇa rākṣasendra mahāvīrya laṅkāsthaḥ svaṃ dhariṣyasi
english: "As long as people endure, so long shall you, Vibhīṣaṇa, O lord of rākṣasas, great in valour, abide in Laṅkā and rule your realm."

sanskrit: prajāḥ saṃrakṣa dharmeṇa nottaraṃ vaktum arhasi
english: "Protect your subjects according to dharma; you need say nothing further."

sanskrit: tam evam uktvā kākutstho hanūmantam athābravīt jīvite kṛtabuddhis tvaṃ mā pratijñāṃ vilopaya
english: Having spoken thus to him, Kākutstha then said to Hanūmat: "You have resolved to live on — do not break the vow you have taken."

sanskrit: matkathāḥ pracariṣyanti yāval loke harīśvara tāvat tvaṃ dhārayan prāṇān pratijñām anupālaya
english: "As long as my stories circulate in the world, O lord of monkeys, so long shall you sustain your life and honour your pledge."

sanskrit: tathaivam uktvā kākutsthaḥ sarvāṃs tān ṛkṣavānarān mayā sārdhaṃ prayāteti tadā tān rāghavo 'bravīt
english: Having spoken thus, Kākutstha then said to all those bears and monkeys: "Come, travel with me" — so did Rāghava address them then.

sanskrit: prabhātāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ pṛthuvakṣā mahāyaśāḥ rāmaḥ kamalapatrākṣaḥ purodhasam athābravīt
english: When night had given way to dawn, broad-chested Rāma of great renown, lotus-eyed, then addressed the chaplain:

sanskrit: agnihotraṃ vrajatv agre sarpir jvalitapāvakam vājapeyātapatraṃ ca śobhayānaṃ mahāpatham
english: "Let the sacred fire of the agnihotra, blazing with clarified butter, proceed ahead, along with the royal parasol of the Vājapeya sacrifice, adorning the great path."

sanskrit: tato vasiṣṭhas tejasvī sarvaṃ niravaśeṣataḥ cakāra vidhivad dharmyaṃ mahāprāsthānikaṃ vidhim
english: Then the radiant Vasiṣṭha performed the entire rite of the Great Departure — the mahāprāsthānika — completely and according to proper injunction.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṣaumāmbaradharo brahma cāvartayan param kuśān gṛhītvā pāṇibhyāṃ prasajya prayayāv atha
english: Then, clad in linen garments and silently reciting the supreme Brahman within, Rāma took kuśa grass in both hands and, inclining forward, set out.

sanskrit: avyāharan kva cit kiṃ cin niśceṣṭo niḥsukhaḥ pathi nirjagāma gṛhāt tasmād dīpyamāno yathāṃśumān
english: Speaking not a word, making no gesture anywhere, beyond pleasure on the path, he went forth from that house blazing like the sun.

sanskrit: rāmasya pārśve savye tu padmā śrīḥ susamāhitā dakṣiṇe hrīr viśālākṣī vyavasāyas tathāgrataḥ
english: On Rāma's left side walked Padmā Śrī, calm and composed; on his right walked Hrī of wide eyes; and Vyavasāya walked ahead of him.

sanskrit: śarā nānāvidhāś cāpi dhanur āyatavigraham anuvrajanti kākutsthaṃ sarve puruṣavigrahāḥ
english: His arrows of various kinds and his bow of elongated form followed Kākutstha, all of them bearing human shapes.

sanskrit: vedā brāhmaṇarūpeṇa sāvitrī sarvarakṣiṇī oṃkāro 'tha vaṣaṭkāraḥ sarve rāmam anuvratāḥ
english: The Vedas in the form of brāhmaṇas, Sāvitrī the all-protecting, Oṃkāra, and Vaṣaṭkāra — all of them followed Rāma in devotion.

sanskrit: ṛṣayaś ca mahātmānaḥ sarva eva mahīsurāḥ anvagacchanta kākutsthaṃ svargadvāram upāgatam
english: The great-souled sages and all the gods of the earth followed Kākutstha as he approached the gate of heaven.

sanskrit: taṃ yāntam anuyānti sma antaḥpuracarāḥ striyaḥ savṛddhabāladāsīkāḥ savarṣavarakiṃkarāḥ
english: The women of the inner palace followed him as he went, along with the elderly, children, and maidservants, and attendants of all ranks and servants bearing tribute.

sanskrit: sāntaḥpuraś ca bharataḥ śatrughnasahito yayau rāmavratam upāgamya rāghavaṃ samanuvratāḥ
english: And Bharata with his inner household, accompanied by Śatrughna, went forth — having embraced Rāma's vow, they followed Rāghava in complete devotion.

sanskrit: tato viprā mahātmānaḥ sāgnihotrāḥ samāhitāḥ saputradārāḥ kākutstham anvagacchan mahāmatim
english: Then the great-souled brāhmaṇas, bearing their sacred fires and composed in mind, followed the highly-minded Kākutstha with their sons and wives.

sanskrit: mantriṇo bhṛtyavargāś ca saputrāḥ sahabāndhavāḥ sānugā rāghavaṃ sarve anvagacchan prahṛṣṭavat
english: The ministers and the ranks of servants, with their sons, kinsmen, and retinues, all followed Rāghava joyfully.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvāḥ prakṛtayo hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanāvṛtāḥ anujagmuḥ pragacchantaṃ rāghavaṃ guṇarañjitāḥ
english: Then all the subjects, surrounded by joyful and prosperous people, followed Rāghava as he went forward, their hearts enraptured by his virtues.

sanskrit: snātaṃ pramuditaṃ sarvaṃ hṛṣṭapuṣpam anuttamam dṛptaṃ kilikilāśabdaiḥ sarvaṃ rāmam anuvratam
english: All had bathed and were joyful, bearing splendid garlands of flowers, proud and resounding with joyful shouts, all following Rāma in devotion.

sanskrit: na tatra kaś cid dīno 'bhūd vrīḍito vāpi duḥkhitaḥ hṛṣṭaṃ pramuditaṃ sarvaṃ babhūva paramādbhutam
english: No one there was wretched, or ashamed, or sorrowful; all were joyful and elated — it was supremely wondrous.

sanskrit: draṣṭukāmo 'tha niryāṇaṃ rājño jānapado janaḥ saṃprāptaḥ so 'pi dṛṣṭvaiva saha sarvair anuvrataḥ
english: Country folk who had come wishing to see the king's departure — they too, upon merely seeing it, followed along together with all the others.

sanskrit: ṛkṣavānararakṣāṃsi janāś ca puravāsinaḥ agachan parayā bhaktyā pṛṣṭhataḥ susamāhitāḥ
english: The bears, monkeys, and rākṣasas, and the citizens of the city, followed behind with supreme devotion, fully composed in mind.
